title: Gidea Park
intro: A garden suburb from 1910–11 on the edge of Romford, with a lake park on the doorstep and north Havering's country parks a short drive or bike ride away. These are the places worth knowing, all within about 5 km of Gidea Park station.

items.name: Raphael Park
items.blurb: Gidea Park's own park: a long lake with a bridge and lakeside promenade, a bandstand, a rockery and wide lawns, named after Herbert Raphael, the landowner behind the garden suburb.
items.tip: Summer theatre plays at the bandstand, and Lodge Farm Park next door adds a playground, tennis courts and a bowling green.

items.name: Reed Pond Walk and Meadway
items.blurb: The heart of the Romford Garden Suburb, built in 1910–11 as an exhibition of Arts and Crafts houses on the old Gidea Hall estate and a conservation area since 1970. Nos. 36 and 38, a pair by M. H. Baillie Scott, are Grade II listed.
items.tip: Make a loop: Reed Pond Walk, then Meadway, where Nos. 16 and 27 are listed exhibition houses, and back along Heath Drive.

items.name: 64 Heath Drive
items.blurb: A white modernist house from the 1934 Modern Homes Exhibition, designed by 26-year-old Francis Skinner, a founder member of Berthold Lubetkin's Tecton group, and Grade II listed. The listed 1911 houses at Nos. 41 and 43 are on the same road.
items.tip: It is a private home: enjoy it from the pavement.

items.name: Langtons Gardens
items.blurb: A Grade II listed Georgian house with landscaped gardens around a serpentine lake, and an orangery, gazebo and bath house from around 1800. It was given to Hornchurch in 1929 on condition that the gardens stay open to everyone.
items.tip: The house is now the borough's register office; the lakeside benches are the quiet spot.

items.name: Havering Country Park
items.blurb: Woods and open grassland on the estate of the medieval royal Palace of Havering, crossed by an avenue of around a hundred giant Wellingtonia redwoods planted in the 19th century to lead up to a house that has since gone.
items.tip: The London LOOP walking route runs through the park if you want a longer walk.

items.name: Bedfords Park
items.blurb: One of Havering's largest parks and a Local Nature Reserve, with a herd of red deer and a south-facing slope that looks out across east London and the Thames to Kent.
items.tip: Climb to the top of the slope on a clear day for the view.

items.name: Dagnam Park
items.blurb: Meadows, ponds and ancient woodland around the site of a vanished manor house, now part of The Manor Local Nature Reserve. Herds of fallow deer graze the quieter fields and the woods fill with bluebells in spring.
items.tip: Go early or late in the day for the best chance of seeing the deer.

items.name: Upminster Windmill
items.blurb: A Grade II* smock mill built in 1803 and one of the finest left in England, restored with new sails and now with a visitor centre and gardens around it.
items.tip: The visitor centre and gardens are free; the mill itself opens on set days with a ticket, so check upminsterwindmill.org first.

items.name: Hornchurch Country Park
items.blurb: The former RAF Hornchurch airfield, a Battle of Britain fighter station, now meadows, scrub and wetland in the Ingrebourne Valley nature reserve. Wartime pillboxes and gun positions still stand along its eastern edge.
items.tip: Start at the Essex Wildlife Trust's Ingrebourne Valley Visitor Centre.
